title: Console workshop — wireframe prioritization & customer synthesis (Aug 2026)
summary: Post-workshop synthesis from Aug 11 design + customer session. Ran a 2.5h wireframe workshop with 6 participants (2 PLG customers, 2 enterprise customers, 2 internal PM/Design). Goal: surface highest-value console improvements that (a) reduce time-to-resolution for latency/cost incidents, (b) make rollouts and routing understandable to SRE/platform teams, and (c) unblock quick self-service optimizations for engineering teams.
objective: Rapidly convert qualitative customer pain points into a ranked backlog of wireframes and prototypes we can validate in 1–2 research sprints.
participants: Asha (facilitator), Jon (design), Elena (research notes), Samir (eng), Priya (PM), customer A (B2B search), customer B (SaaS analytics), customer C (platform team), customer D (early PLG)
method_notes: Agenda: 1) 20m customer pain lightning, 2) 30m sketching round (small groups), 3) 40m impact/effort affinity card sort, 4) 20m dot-vote and backlog mapping, 5) 10m action owners. Artifacts captured in confluence link above + whiteboard photos in Slack thread #console-workshop-aug.
raw_customer_pain_highlights:
- Hard to tell which model variant served requests during an incident
- No quick way to compare token cost pre/post-release
- Rollout controls are buried and hard to audit (who kicked a canary, when)
- Need to test routing policies on a small subset before full rollout
- Observability (traces + token counts) often requires stitching multiple screens
- 'Preset' tuning suggestions would be helpful for teams without infra bandwidth
wireframe-priorities:
Dot-vote prioritized list (top->bottom):
1) Route-level realtime breakdown (latency, token count, model variant drilldown) — 14 votes
2) Rollout timeline with audit trail + quick rollback button — 12 votes
3) Preset optimization cards (cost, latency, quality) with one-click apply — 9 votes
4) Canary playground (simulate routing on sample traffic) — 7 votes
5) Inline experiment results & regression flags for prompt sets — 6 votes
6) Compact model catalog compare modal (perf/quantization/cost) — 4 votes
wireframe-notes:
Route-level panel: top-level KPIs, heatmap of 95p latency over time, model variant stacked area showing percentage of tokens by variant. Drilldown reveals recent commits/versions and link to deployment.
Rollout timeline: show canary windows, % traffic, owner, linked rollout policy. Add 'sweep' control: increase/decrease canary by predefined increments. Include confirmation modal that shows fallback path.
Presets: simple cards (Latency-focused, Cost-focused, Balanced). Each card lists expected delta (tokens/sec, estimated $/100k tokens), linked test suite. UX: show 'preview changes' before apply.
Canary playground: small sandbox toggle that runs sample traffic through routing rules without affecting production; show sample outputs and token counts. Needs strong guardrails (quota limit, owner approval).
quick_wins:
- Add a model-variant label to request logs view (low dev effort) — ticket CR-4521
- Surface 'last modified by' on rollout cards (small backend + UI work) — owner: Jon, due: 2026-09-02
- Expose preset suggestions in route creation flow (copy + quick apply) — prototype in Figma by Aug 26
medium_scope_items:
- Route-level realtime breakdown (requires metrics backend work + UI) — spike in eng: 1 week, design: 3 days
- Rollout timeline with audit trail and rollback — backend work to store audit events + UI timeline component
- Canary playground (policy simulator) — considered a gated feature for Dedicated customers first
risky_assumptions:
- Customers want 'one-click' presets; risk: teams may prefer custom tuning for regulatory reasons. Validate with 3 follow-up interviews.
- Canary playground might be used as a crutch (bypass infra approvals); need RBAC constraints.
- Real-time breakdown feasibility depends on current metrics sample rate (SRE to confirm).
decisions_and_tradeoffs:
- Prioritize route-level KPIs and rollout timeline for Q4. Rationale: highest impact on incident MTTR and auditability.
- Delay full canary playground to pilot with 2 customers (Dedicated) to limit blast radius.
- Presets to ship as read-only recommendations in hosted GA, writeable for Dedicated customers in next phase.

open_questions:
- How much historical data do customers expect in the route-level heatmap? (7d/30d/90d)
- Do legal/compliance teams require immutable audit logs for rollouts (append-only)?
- What quota limits make sense for a sandboxed canary playground?
- Is the cost estimate for presets accurate across quantized/model variants?

notes_to_self: Keep language developer-first: show token counts and sample outputs. Avoid marketing-y labels in product copy. Validate presets with at least one non-infra engineer. Consider privacy implications of storing sample traffic in sandbox.

ux_research_plan: Quick validation plan: recruit 3 customers (mix of PLG and enterprise) for 45m remote sessions. Tasks: 1) find model variant for incident, 2) locate rollout history and initiate rollback, 3) apply a preset and observe estimated cost change. Success metrics: task completion rate >80%, time-to-complete median <4m for tasks 1+2, qualitative satisfaction score >6/10.
final_comments: This is an actionable groomed set of priorities — not final. We should treat the next 2 sprints as validation sprints rather than implementation sprints. Keep backlog lean: focus on observable MTTR reductions and auditability improvements.
